chunks: And what Safwan narrated from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying:
"Indeed, I pray the Night Prayer, finish it, then pray the two rak'ahs, and sleep as Allah wills before the dawn rises. If I wake up at dawn, I repeat them."
For these two reports refer to one who prayed these two rak'ahs while a portion of the night remained before the first dawn rose; in that case, it is appropriate for him to repeat the two rak'ahs.
It is also possible that Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both) repeated them as a recommended act (not obligatory).
And in the two reports is not [stated] that when you do that and the matter is upon that state, you must repeat them a second time [obligatorily].
As for the recitation in them, it has been narrated...

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: The two rak'ahs (specifically the pre-dawn voluntary prayers)

ai.seo_question: Do I need to repeat the two pre-dawn prayers if I sleep through the first dawn?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the status of the two voluntary rak'ahs prayed before Fajr when one sleeps through the first dawn; the Imams' practice suggests that repeating them is recommended (istihbab) rather than obligatory, as the texts do not explicitly command a second repetition. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding night prayers and the distinction between the two dawns, emphasizing that the initial prayer remains valid even if interrupted by sleep until the second dawn. The discussion also touches upon the recitation within these specific rak'ahs, reinforcing their status as distinct voluntary acts of worship.
